sources.title: Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications
How Google interprets the robots.txt specification
How to specify a canonical URL with rel=canonical and other methods
How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers
Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search
Tell Google about localized versions of your page

findings.title: Sitemap audit is presence-only; lastmod:new Date() teaches Google to ignore lastmod
findings.why_it_ranks: A sitemap is a weak canonical hint and a discovery list, not a ranking score. Google (build-sitemap, still current 2026-09-11) wants only the URLs you want in results: absolute HTTPS canonicals that return 200, are indexable, and are not redirects. Google uses lastmod only when it is consistently and verifiably accurate (real content change, not a rebuild). Google ignores changefreq and priority. Inaccurate lastmod causes Google to drop the signal for the whole file. Crawl-budget (2026-07-22): keep the sitemap limited to what you want crawled.
findings.nextjs_how: In app/sitemap.ts set lastModified from real content dates (glossary updatedAt, MDX frontmatter, CMS publishedAt). Never lastModified: new Date(). Omit changeFrequency and priority. List only public indexable routes. After host lock, every loc must match metadataBase. Next MetadataRoute.Sitemap also supports alternates.languages for hreflang in the same file.
findings.seoBoost_gap: runDomainChecks (lib/scanner.ts:1421-1448) counts <loc>, notes any <lastmod>, and marks good. It never: (1) HEAD/GET each loc for 200 vs 3xx/4xx, (2) drop noindex or cross-canonical locs, (3) require loc host == page canonical host, (4) flag identical lastmod across all URLs (build stamp), (5) follow sitemapindex children, (6) ignore changefreq/priority as non-signals. Product app/sitemap.ts:8-11 stamps new Date() plus monthly/weekly + priority 0.7–1.0 on every glossary term. robots.ts Sitemap: is https://seoboost.app/sitemap.xml while root canonical is https://boost-seo.vercel.app — two different preferred-URL lists.
findings.verify_how: 1) Scan this repo: sitemap check must warning 'lastmod identical / build stamp', not lastmod ✓. 2) Fixture sitemap with a 301 loc, a noindex loc, and an off-host loc → each listed, status warning/critical. 3) After sitemap.ts fix, lastModified differs per URL and matches a real date. 4) GSC Sitemaps: no 'Submitted URL marked noindex' / redirect errors.

findings.title: Canonical checker strips http/www/slash so it cannot see the host split this site ships
findings.why_it_ranks: Google (consolidate-duplicate-urls, updated 2026-07-10) ranks signals: 301/308 redirect > rel=canonical > sitemap inclusion. Do include a self-referential canonical on the chosen URL. Prefer HTTPS. Do not name different URLs via different methods. Trailing-slash and www variants are separate URLs until one 301s. Google may still pick another canonical; URL Inspection is ground truth.
findings.nextjs_how: One production origin (likely https://seoboost.app). Root metadataBase + relative alternates.canonical per route. 301 http→https and www↔apex in next.config redirects or the host. Pick trailingSlash (default false) and let Next 301 the other form. Absolute canonicals only. Do not put a site-wide absolute canonical in root layout that children forget to override.
findings.seoBoost_gap: analysePage (lib/scanner.ts:400-407) rewrites http→https, strips www, strips trailing slashes, then compares. http vs https, www vs apex, and /page vs /page/ therefore pass as 'Valid self-referencing canonical'. Relative canonicals fail against the absolute page URL. Link: rel=canonical headers are unread. Multiple rel=canonical tags use only the first. Product: app/layout.tsx:27-29 metadataBase + canonical = https://boost-seo.vercel.app; app/pricing/layout.tsx canonical /pricing resolves onto that Vercel host; app/sitemap.ts and app/robots.ts prefer https://seoboost.app; glossary generateMetadata canonical is the literal /glossary/${termData.slug} (08-04). Conflicting methods on one page.
findings.verify_how: 1) Fixture http://www.example.com/foo/ with canonical https://example.com/foo → must warn scheme + www + slash, not good. 2) Self-scan: canonical host must equal sitemap loc host. 3) View-source /glossary/canonical-tag: rel=canonical is https://<origin>/glossary/canonical-tag, not a ${} string. 4) Lighthouse canonical audit on the collected URL must not fail cross-host.

findings.title: fetchUrl drops every non-200; 301/308 vs 307 and soft 404s never become checks
findings.why_it_ranks: Google (http-network-errors, 2026-02-04; redirects, 2026-04-14) uses status as the indexation switch. 200/2xx: content may be indexed (soft 404 if the body is an error). 301 and 308: strong permanent canonical signal. 302/303/307: temporary; source URL can stay in results. Crawlers follow ~10 hops; chains waste budget. 404/410: drop from index, recrawl less. 5xx/429: slow the host, keep old URLs until they persist. JS SEO (2026-03-04): rendering is queued for 200s and may be skipped on non-200.
findings.nextjs_how: Use notFound() for missing slugs (real 404). Permanent moves: next.config redirects with statusCode 301 or 308, or permanentRedirect(). next/navigation redirect() is 307 — wrong for retired URLs. Auth gates: 401/403 or 307 to login is fine; do not 301 a dashboard to login. Add app/not-found.tsx that still returns 404.
findings.seoBoost_gap: fetchUrl (lib/scanner.ts:285) returns null on !res.ok. Default fetch follows redirects, so the recorded status is the final 200 and hop count is lost. scanDomain (1630) continues. No check ids for 404/410, 5xx, 429, hop>=3, 301 vs 307, or 200+'not found' soft 404. Product: no app/not-found.tsx. dashboard/page.tsx:19 redirect('/seo-audit-login') is 307. Glossary unknown slugs do call notFound() (good) but generateMetadata on miss only sets a title — if notFound were skipped, that would be a soft 404.
findings.verify_how: 1) Fetch with redirect:'manual' on a 301 fixture: record status 301, hops, finalUrl. 2) Nav link to /missing → source page broken-internal 404 (with 08-12). 3) 200 page titled '404' / 'Not Found' with thin main → soft-404 critical. 4) curl -I /dashboard unauthenticated → 307, not 301. 5) Missing glossary slug → 404, not 200.

findings.title: robots.txt vs meta robots vs X-Robots-Tag conflicts are unaudited; login is indexable
findings.why_it_ranks: robots.txt controls fetch, not indexation (intro, 2025-12-10). noindex (meta or X-Robots-Tag) removes a URL only if the crawler can fetch it (block-indexing; robots-meta-tag, 2026-03-24). Disallow + noindex = crawler never sees noindex → URL-only listing if linked. noindex is not valid in robots.txt (Google dropped it). Conflicting meta + header: most restrictive wins. nosnippet also blocks AI Overviews / AI Mode as a direct input (2026-03-24).
findings.nextjs_how: app/robots.ts: Disallow only paths you never want fetched (/api/, /_next/data is optional — do not Disallow /_next/static or CSS/JS or Google cannot render). Utility/auth pages: allow crawl + metadata.robots = { index: false, follow: false } (or X-Robots-Tag). Password-protect /dashboard. Do not Disallow a URL you need de-indexed. Trailing-slash Disallow:/dashboard/ does not match /dashboard.
findings.seoBoost_gap: meta-robots (lib/scanner.ts:430-454) reads only meta[name=robots] + one x-robots-tag. It ignores name=googlebot. Any noindex is critical — including correct noindex on /sign-up. Page-level nofollow is warned as equity loss (hint, not a command). Domain robots check never diffs Disallow prefixes vs sitemap locs vs on-page noindex. Product: app/robots.ts Disallow /dashboard/, /api/, /auth/ but footer still links /dashboard (08-06). /seo-audit-login/layout.tsx robots index:true on a 'use client' login. /sign-up/layout.tsx is noindex,nofollow (correct, and not Disallow'd). Root layout index:true inherits onto /dashboard if Google ever fetches /dashboard (Disallow:/dashboard/ may not match /dashboard).
findings.verify_how: 1) Fixture: Disallow /thin/ plus meta noindex on /thin → critical 'noindex unreachable'. 2) Fixture: googlebot-only noindex, empty robots meta → must still detect. 3) /seo-audit-login view-source: noindex. 4) robots.txt Disallow includes /dashboard and /dashboard/. 5) Self-scan must not mark /sign-up noindex as a money-page critical.

findings.title: Cheerio-only crawl misses RSC/client shells, render queue rules, and Next soft 404s
findings.why_it_ranks: Googlebot (JS SEO, 2026-03-04) crawls, then queues 200s for WRS unless the initial HTML/header is noindex — in which case it may skip JavaScript. Non-200 responses may skip render entirely. Soft 404s (200 + error body) stay in the crawl queue (crawl-budget, 2026-07-22). Client-only titles, canonicals, or noindex toggles are unsafe. History API URLs are crawlable; hash routes are not.
findings.nextjs_how: Keep indexable content in Server Components / generateMetadata so the first HTML has title, canonical, robots, H1, and links. Call notFound() on empty dynamic data. Do not ship a default noindex in root HTML and remove it in useEffect. Prefer RSC over an SPA shell. app/not-found.tsx for the 404 URL Google should recrawl less.
findings.seoBoost_gap: scanDomain never renders. A 'use client' page with empty first HTML scores as thin/missing-title. A 200 not-found UI can still pass word-count from chrome. No check for hash routing, empty #root, or initial noindex that JS clears. Product login is 'use client' (app/seo-audit-login/page.tsx) with robots in the sibling layout (SSR tags exist — lucky). Homepage H1 lives in a client motion component (02-03). No not-found.tsx. User-Agent is SEOScanBot/2.0, not Googlebot, so Next htmlLimitedBots streaming can hide metadata from the scanner while Googlebot sees it (09-08).
findings.verify_how: 1) Fixture CSR shell (empty main, title set in useEffect) → critical 'content not in first HTML; confirm URL Inspection / Rich Results URL mode'. 2) Fixture 200 + h1 'Page not found' → soft-404, not a word-count warning. 3) Fixture initial noindex + JS index → warn 'Google may never run that JS'. 4) Disable JS on / : H1 still present after 02-03.

findings.title: Pagination, infinite scroll, and faceted URLs are skipped — not audited
findings.why_it_ranks: Google's pagination guide (still posted 2026-09-11): unique URL per page (?page=n), self-canonical on each page (do not canonicalize page 2+ to page 1), sequential crawlable <a href> next/prev, link back to page 1 of the collection, no #fragments for page numbers (ignored). rel=next/prev is unused by Google. Infinite scroll / Load more: Google does not click buttons; expose paginated hrefs or a sitemap. Facets/sort (?order=price, filter=): noindex or robots.txt Disallow so they do not explode inventory. Do not put those variants in the sitemap.
findings.nextjs_how: searchParams pages: generateMetadata with a self canonical including ?page=n (or a /page/n segment). Render <Link href={`?page=${n+1}`}> not onClick. Faceted routes: robots index:false or Disallow /?sort= /?filter= and canonical to the clean category URL. prefetch={false} on huge lists is UX only (08-11).
findings.seoBoost_gap: PROGRAMMATIC_PATTERNS (lib/scanner.ts:192-198) skips /page/\d+, /tag/, and ?filter|sort|order|min_price. Those URLs never get canonical/robots/sitemap checks. No ids for: page-2 canonicalized to page-1, missing sequential <a href>, hash pagination, facet URLs in sitemap, infinite-scroll with no crawlable next. howToFix never states that Google dropped rel=next/prev.
findings.verify_how: Fixture /cat?page=2 with canonical /cat → warning 'paginated URL must self-canonicalize'. Fixture Load more <button> with no <a href> to page 2 → warning. Fixture sitemap listing /cat?sort=price → sitemap-quality warning (06-01). Do not skip these URLs when they appear as sitemap locs (08-03).

findings.title: hreflang check is x-default-only; no next-intl / [locale] reciprocity audit
findings.why_it_ranks: Google (localized-versions, 2025-12-22): every language/region URL must list the full set, including itself, plus x-default. Annotations must be reciprocal. Use hreflang on HTML, HTTP header, or sitemap xhtml:link — pick one consistent method. Canonical in a cluster should be the same-language URL (consolidate-duplicate-urls, 2026-07-10). Wrong codes or one-way links are ignored. html lang is not a substitute.
findings.nextjs_how: App Router: app/[locale]/... + generateStaticParams. generateMetadata.alternates.languages + x-default. next-intl or next.config i18n must 308/301 to the prefixed locale, not rewrite silently. Sitemap localizations[] (Next 14.2+) or xhtml:link. Do not mix /de and ?lang=de as two indexable URLs.
findings.seoBoost_gap: hreflang (lib/scanner.ts:959-977) runs only if tags already exist, and only tests x-default. No reciprocal pair check, no valid BCP-47 lint, no sitemap hreflang, no html[lang] vs hreflang mismatch, no 'locale URLs exist without annotations'. Reference URL is wrong: .../international/localization (404-class). Repo has no [locale] tree (single-locale is fine) but the product cannot audit customer next-intl sites. 08-08 already noted locale prefixes as IA; this lane owns annotation correctness.
findings.verify_how: Fixture /en and /de each with only a self hreflang → warning 'not reciprocal'. Fixture both + x-default → good. Fixture /en/pricing + /de/pricing and zero tags → warning. Fix reference to localized-versions. Single-locale SeoBoost: no hreflang warning.

findings.title: Next.js trailingSlash, basePath, and middleware SEO traps are invisible
findings.why_it_ranks: Next default trailingSlash:false 301s /about/ → /about. skipTrailingSlashRedirect makes both 200 — duplicate URLs unless a canonical or Proxy redirect exists. basePath prefixes every public URL; robots.ts, sitemap.ts, and metadataBase that omit it invent a second site. Middleware rewrites (200) hide the real path from the user and from Google; Google indexes the requested URL. Geo/locale middleware that 307-loops or serves the same body on / and /en splits signals. matcher that blocks /_next/static breaks rendering.
findings.nextjs_how: Set trailingSlash explicitly. Keep automatic slash redirects unless you handle them in Proxy. If basePath is '/app', metadataBase must include it and sitemap locs must too. Middleware: NextResponse.redirect for URL changes (301/308), NextResponse.rewrite only for internal aliases you do not want indexed separately. Never geo-rewrite without a distinct URL + hreflang.
findings.seoBoost_gap: normaliseUrl (lib/scanner.ts:229-233) strips trailing slashes before analysis, so dual-200 slash variants collapse to one visit. No detection of basePath, x-middleware-rewrite, or next.config trailingSlash. Repo: next.config.ts has neither trailingSlash nor basePath and there is no middleware.ts (safe today). Scanner still cannot coach customer Next apps that do have them. Root Cache-Control immutable on / (.*) (02-11) also freezes HTML Googlebot recrawls.
findings.verify_how: 1) Request /pricing and /pricing/ on a trailingSlash:false host: one 200, one 308/301. 2) Fixture skipTrailingSlashRedirect both 200 → warning 'choose one slash + 301'. 3) Fixture sitemap loc without basePath while pages live under /docs → host/path mismatch. 4) Response header x-middleware-rewrite on an indexable URL → warning 'rewrite indexed as requested URL'.

findings.title: robots.txt parser is * + prefix-only and misstates what Disallow does
findings.why_it_ranks: Google's REP (robots-txt-spec): most specific path wins; on a tie, least restrictive (Allow beats Disallow of equal length). Wildcards * and $ are supported. Group by user-agent; Googlebot uses the longest matching group (Googlebot, then *). robots.txt 5xx is retried; a 200 HTML body is not a valid robots file. Disallow does not de-index. Disallow of JS/CSS stops rendering. Crawl-delay is ignored by Google.
findings.nextjs_how: Keep app/robots.ts specific. Allow /_next/static. Disallow both /dashboard and /dashboard/. Sitemap: absolute URL on the canonical host. Do not emit noindex in robots.txt. Optional: Google-Extended / AdsBot groups only if you intend them.
findings.seoBoost_gap: Parser (lib/scanner.ts:1381-1392) lowercases the file, reads only user-agent: *, ignores Allow exceptions and * $ rules, then crawl uses pathname.startsWith(prefix) — Disallow:/dashboard/ does not skip /dashboard. Missing robots (including 403/5xx, because fetchUrl nulls !res.ok) is a warning that 10-08 lists as a false-positive ranking claim. blocksEverything copy (1397) says Disallow:/ 'completely removes your site from Google search results' — false; URLs can still appear as listings. No check for Disallow /_next/, /static, .js, .css. Product robots.ts paths use trailing slashes only.
findings.verify_how: 1) Fixture Allow: /dashboard/report + Disallow: /dashboard/ → /dashboard/report is crawlable. 2) Disallow: /*.json$ respected. 3) Disallow: /_next/ → critical 'rendering resources blocked'. 4) 403 robots.txt → 'unreachable', not 'Missing'. 5) Copy must not say Disallow removes the site from the index.

findings.title: X-Robots-Tag, googlebot meta, and Link canonical headers are only half-read
findings.why_it_ranks: Google treats meta robots and X-Robots-Tag as equivalent (robots-meta-tag, 2026-03-24). Headers are the only way to noindex PDFs/images. Multiple X-Robots-Tag lines combine; most restrictive wins. rel=canonical may be a Link HTTP header (PDF/non-HTML). googlebot / googlebot-news metas are first-class. unavailable_after is a dated noindex. max-snippet:0 equals nosnippet and limits AI Overview input.
findings.nextjs_how: HTML routes: Metadata API robots (+ googleBot max-image-preview/large already in root). Non-HTML: next.config headers() X-Robots-Tag. Do not set a sitewide X-Robots-Tag: noindex on / (.*) — that would noindex the whole site. Prefer one canonical method (HTML link, not both HTML and Link header).
findings.seoBoost_gap: x-robots-tag is a single lowercased header (last Set-Cookie-style overwrite if the runtime concatenates poorly). googlebot meta unread. Link response header unread. No unavailable_after / none / noimageindex coaching. Root next.config.ts headers() has no X-Robots-Tag (good) but also no way for the scanner to warn if a CDN injects one. howToFix still recommends <meta name="robots" content="index, follow"> which is a no-op (all is default).
findings.verify_how: Fixture X-Robots-Tag: noindex plus meta index,follow → noindex wins, not 'good'. Fixture <meta name=googlebot content=noindex> only → detected. Fixture Link: <https://ex.com/a>; rel="canonical" with no HTML canonical → pass as header canonical. Sitewide X-Robots-Tag noindex → critical.

findings.title: Product indexation hygiene: indexable login, 307 auth, missing not-found, split Sitemap host
findings.why_it_ranks: Google indexes 200 HTML it is allowed to fetch. A login URL with index:true can rank as a thin result. A 307 from /dashboard to login is a temporary signal (keeps /dashboard if it were crawlable). Missing app/not-found.tsx relies on the framework default; custom soft-looking 404s are a GSC class. robots Sitemap: on a different host than the property Google crawled is a cross-submit case, not automatic discovery.
findings.nextjs_how: 1) seo-audit-login + any /sign-in alias: robots index:false. 2) not-found.tsx with a real 404 status. 3) robots.ts Sitemap: and sitemap.ts locs on the same origin as metadataBase. 4) Disallow both /dashboard and /dashboard/; remove footer links to /dashboard (08-10). 5) Keep sign-up noindex and crawlable.
findings.seoBoost_gap: app/seo-audit-login/layout.tsx:6-8 index:true. app/sign-up/layout.tsx already noindex. No not-found.tsx. app/robots.ts:10 Sitemap seoboost.app vs layout canonical vercel.app. Footer Documentation / Instant Reports → /dashboard (app/page.tsx). Scanner would currently fail a correct login noindex as critical (06-04).
findings.verify_how: curl -s /seo-audit-login | rg -i 'noindex'. curl -I /this-is-not-a-page → 404. robots.txt Sitemap host == canonical host. Self-scan: login noindex is informational/good, not critical.

findings.title: Crawl-budget copy treats folder depth and Disallow as ranking switches
findings.why_it_ranks: Google (crawl-budget, 2026-07-22): this guide is for ~1M moderately changing URLs or ~10k+ changing daily, or heavy 'Discovered – currently not indexed'. Hostload is per hostname (www ≠ apex ≠ vercel.app). Budget levers: shrink duplicate inventory, robots-block URL explosions you do not want fetched, 404/410 removed pages (not Disallow — blocked URLs stay in the queue longer), kill soft 404s, accurate lastmod, short redirect chains, fast render. noindex still spends a fetch. Google will not automatically spend freed budget elsewhere unless already at capacity.
findings.nextjs_how: Do not engineer crawl budget on a marketing site this small. Do teach customers: 404/410 deleted URLs; robots-block facet explosions; never Disallow JS/CSS; never noindex+Disallow. Click depth is 08-02, not path-segment count.
findings.seoBoost_gap: url-structure (lib/scanner.ts:478-482) says URLs >4 folders 'receive less crawl budget'. robots-txt critical copy says Disallow:/ removes the site from results (06-09). No mention of the 10k/1M threshold, per-hostname budget, 404 vs Disallow for deletions, or 304 Not Modified. ssl howToFix still only shows Apache/Nginx 301, not next.config redirects.
findings.verify_how: Copy review: zero claims that folder depth spends crawl budget. Disallow:/ message = 'blocks crawling; URLs may still list'. Sites under 10k URLs: crawl-budget check is info, not critical, unless soft-404/facet explosion is detected.

must_implement_now: 06-02: Stop stripping scheme/www/slash in the canonical compare; lock one origin across metadataBase, canonical, sitemap locs, and robots Sitemap: (with 03-03).
06-01: Sitemap quality — only 200/indexable/same-host locs; flag identical lastmod; stop lastModified: new Date() in app/sitemap.ts; drop changefreq/priority coaching.
06-03: Record status, hops, and soft 404s in fetchUrl (redirect:'manual'); add app/not-found.tsx; do not 301 auth gates.
06-04: Detect Disallow+noindex collisions; noindex /seo-audit-login; treat utility noindex as good; Disallow /dashboard and /dashboard/.
06-05: First-HTML vs empty-shell / soft-404 checks; never tell users JS can undo an initial noindex.
conflicts_to_avoid: Do not use robots.txt Disallow to de-index a URL. Allow the crawl and serve noindex (or password-protect).
Do not combine Disallow and noindex on the same path. The crawler will never see the noindex.
Do not treat lastModified: new Date() or changefreq/priority as sitemap quality. Google ignores the latter and distrusts fake lastmod.
Do not canonicalize paginated page 2+ to page 1. Each page needs its own URL and self-canonical. Google no longer uses rel=next/rel=prev.
Do not recommend page-level or internal nofollow for PageRank sculpting (08-06, crawl-budget 2026-07-22). Remove the link or robots-block fetch.
Do not use next/navigation redirect() (307) for permanent URL changes. Use permanentRedirect or next.config 301/308.
Do not Disallow /_next/static, CSS, or JS. Google skips rendering blocked resources.
Do not claim crawl-budget engineering is required under ~10k rapidly changing URLs. Folder depth is not click depth (08-02).
Do not add a second sitemap XML parser. Extend the one 08-03/07-02/09-09 will share. 06 owns loc quality (status, noindex, host, lastmod honesty).
Do not add a second fetchUrl status recorder. 06-03, 08-12, and 09-03 consume one hop/status object.
Do not mark every noindex as critical. Auth, thank-you, faceted, and search pages should pass when noindex is intentional.
Do not pick a different production host than 03-03 / 10-03. Schema, OG, sitemap, and canonical must move together.
Do not overwrite sibling findings JSON.
cross_agent_notes: Siblings read: 00-cross-notes.json, 02-core-web-vitals.json, 03-structured-data.json, 05-content-eeat.json, 07-media-seo.json, 08-internal-linking.json, 09-product-gap-competitors.json, 10-verification-harness.json. 01 and 04 were not in the folder.

00 merge: sitemap parse is owned by 08-03 (HTML <loc> seed). 06-01 adds quality gates on that parse (200, indexable, same-host, lastmod honesty). 07-02/07-08 attach image:image / video:video. 09-09 is the competitor-shaped lastmod-stamp check — same id surface as 06-01, do not ship sitemap-honesty twice.

03-03 / 10-03 / 09-07: one origin. 06-02 is the crawl-signal version (canonical vs sitemap vs robots Sitemap: vs redirects). Wait for metadata lane 01/04 before coding the host. Do not 'fix' sitemap to vercel.app if 03 picks seoboost.app.

08-01/08-03/08-12: orphans and click depth need status-aware fetches. 06-03 owns Google status semantics (301/308 vs 307, 10 hops, 404/410 vs Disallow, soft 404). 08-12 owns broken-internal on the source page. One FetchResult { status, hops, finalUrl, headers, html }.

08-08 locale prefixes vs 06-07 hreflang: 08 detects /en/ folders; 06 validates reciprocity, x-default, sitemap xhtml:link, next-intl. 08-04 escaped glossary canonical is a 06-02 verify case after they unescape.

09-01/09-03/09-10: JS render, dropped 4xx, Next soft 404. 06-05 states the 2026-03-04 render-queue rules (200 queued; noindex may skip JS; non-200 may skip render). 09 owns competitor table + Chromium pass. Do not add a second headless lane in 06.

05-01 skips /author/ via PROGRAMMATIC_PATTERNS — same skip list 06-06 uses for /page/N and facets. When 08-03 seeds sitemap locs, do not skip those locs even if the pattern matches (08 conflicts_to_avoid). 05-04 wants /login usually noindex — 06-04/06-11.
02-11 Cache-Control immutable on HTML fights recrawl freshness; not a 06 check id. 02-03 client H1 is a first-HTML risk 06-05 will flag if the H1 is absent from the raw document.

10-06 will GET /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml in CI. Align assertions with 06-01/06-11 (host match, no dashboard locs, no changefreq asserts). 10-08 false-positive list: missing robots/sitemap must stay optional/hint after 06-09 copy fix.
07-02: do not enqueue image file URLs as HTML pages when validating sitemap locs.
